h: What to know before you clip in
p: Clip 'n Climb is one of those activities that looks scarier from the ground than it feels once you're on the wall. The auto-belay does the hard work of keeping you safe, so the only thing you need to bring is a bit of nerve. First-timers often start on the easier walls to build confidence, then move on to the more daring challenges once they've got the hang of letting go and being lowered down.

Parents, don't just stand at the side. Climbing alongside your kids is a great way to encourage them, and they'll love trying to beat you to the top. Spectating grown-ups can usually watch the action, so if not everyone wants to climb, they can still come along and cheer. It pays to arrive a little early so you're ready for the safety briefing without any rush.

There's a lot more to Colchester beyond the castle, so it's easy to build a bigger day out. Colchester Zoo, out at Stanway on the edge of town, is a big family favourite with animals from all over the world. Nature lovers can head to High Woods Country Park, a large green space with woodland, meadows and a lake, ideal for a picnic after a morning on the walls. If you fancy the coast, Mersea Island is a short drive south, known for its oysters, beach huts and tidal causeway. And to the north, the gentle countryside of Dedham Vale, made famous by John Constable's paintings, is perfect for a peaceful riverside walk.
